ened, paralysed, petrified, poisoned
Senses darkvision 60 ft., passive Perception 10
Languages understands the languages of the creature that is
attuned to it but can’t speak
Challenge 1/2 (100 XP)
Afterburners. The wyvern can use a bonus action to expend 1
charge and double its flying speed until the start of its next turn.
Fuel. Over the course of 8 hours (which can be done as part of a
long rest), the wyvern can consume high-quality charcoal worth
at least 1 gp to regain 1d4 + 2 expended charges. If the wyvern
drops to 0 charges, it falls prone and unconscious until it is
recharged in this manner.
Immutable Form. The wyvern is immune to any spell or effect that
would alter its form.
Magic Resistance. The wyvern has advantage on saving throws
against spells and other magical effects.
Actions
Mechanical Claw. Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one
target. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing damage.
Dragonling Breath. The wyvern expends 3 charges and exhales
fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a DC 13
Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) fire damage on a failed
save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
Reconstitute. The wyvern expends 1 charge, regaining 2d6 + 3 hit
points.
Clockwork Wyvern
Clockwork Wyvern
Wondrous item, rare (requires attunement)
Component: construct lifespark
This limited edition clockwork wyvern comes with a fully
operational, miniature coal engine. Thanks to an intricate
mix of steam-powered gears and pistons, the construct
has lifelike movements and mannerisms. Unlike its non-
magical cousins, this particular specimen gains a degree
of self-awareness when a creature attunes to it.
Combat. In combat, the clockwork wyvern shares
your initiative count, but takes its turn immediately after
yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but
the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action,
unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command
it to take an action in its stat block or the Dash, Disen-
gage, Help, Hide, or Search action. The wyvern has 6
charges; see the wyvern’s stat block for details on how it
can expend and recharge this resource.
Death and Damage. If the clockwork wyvern is
reduced to 0 hit points, it loses all charges and becomes
inert. A wyvern that has 0 hit points regains 1 hit point
when it takes lightning damage from a spell of 1st level
or higher, or if 2 gp of charcoal is placed in its chest-fur-
nace. The clockwork wyvern regains 2d6 hit points each
time the mending cantrip is cast on it. Except for these
two means or its Reconstitute action, a wyvern can’t
regain hit points.
Clockwork
Wyvern

Actions

Grab. Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16
(3d6 + 6) bludgeoning damage and the target is grappled (escape

Bash. The ape takes two creatures grappled by it and savagely

DC 17 Constitution saving throw. A creature takes 25 (3d12 + 6)

Each creature in the line must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving
throw, taking 13 (3d8) fire damage and 13 (3d8) radiant damage
on a failure, or half as much damage on a success. If the ape starts
its turn in direct sunlight, this action automatically recharges.
Jade Skull of the Sun King
Jade Skull of the Sun King
Wondrous item, rare (requires attunement by a spellcaster)
Component: pouch of celestial (couatl) feathers
This jade skull wears the crown of a fallen Sun King.
Legend says that each king had to prove themselves
worthy of the blessing of a couatl so that they may craft
their own crown from its gifted feathers. The stories also
tell of the power stored in these precious artefacts, and of
the hubris of thieves. Those for whom the crowns were
not intended are subject to bestial curses should they try
to don these royal raiments.
This item has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended
charges daily at dawn.
Vestigial Radiance. While holding the skull, you can
use an action to cast the sacred flame and dancing lights
cantrips, using your spell save DC.
Blazing Eyes. As an action, you can brandish the skull
in front of you, speak its command word, and expend 1
charge to cast the scorching ray spell (3rd-level), which
uses your spell attack modifier and deals radiant damage
instead of fire damage.
Curse. Removing the crown from the jade skull curses
the last creature that touched the crown until it’s once again
placed upon the jade skull. While cursed, the skull’s mag-
ical properties are suppressed, and the crown appears
on the head of the cursed creature and transforms it
into an accursed feathered ape (see below), multi-
coloured like a couatl, using the ape’s game statis-
tics instead of its own. The ape is unwilling to
part with the crown and is hostile towards any
creature that it can see within 60 feet. When
the curse ends, the creature reverts back
to its original form and gains 2 levels of
exhaustion. This curse can be removed
from this item by the wish spell or a
deal with a couatl.
Jade Skull of
the Sun King

that isn’t protected from divination magic. It growls gently in the
direction to warn its owner.

tinguishable from a normal head of garlic.

direction from which their scent comes.

ing powder in a 30-foot radius. For the next 8 hours, any non-gar-
lycanthrope creature that passes through the area has disadvan-

Garlycanthrope
Garlycanthrope
Wondrous item, uncommon
Component: plant poison gland
Originally commissioned by an infamous vampire hunt-
ress, Dr. Francis N. Stein’s garlycanthropes have proved
themselves the ‘must-have commodity of the season’
for monster hunters everywhere. Their ability to detect
undead and shapechangers has saved many potential
victims from the jaws of a mimic, or from walking into a
vampire’s lair.
Animate Bulb. As a bonus action while holding this
item, you can speak its command word. In response, this
inanimate bulb of garlic becomes a creature that uses
the garlycanthrope stat block, sprouting little legs, eyes,
and a panting muzzle. It is extremely friendly to you
and your allies, but is skittish if any of them are undead
or shapechangers. In combat, the garlycanthrope shares
your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately
after yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own,
but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge
action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to
command it to take one of the actions in its stat block or
the Dash, Disengage, Help, Hide, or Search action.
After 1 hour, or if the garlycanthrope is reduced to 0
hit points, it becomes an inanimate bulb of garlic once
more. Once this property of the item has been used, it
can’t be used again until the next dawn. Be careful not to
eat it in the meantime!

apart the barriers between worlds, summoning primor-
dial avatars of air, earth, fire, and water from the chaotic
depths of the Elemental Planes. When this fails misera-
bly, the magic can produce an elemental mote instead,

Pitcrow
Denizens of the Hells, pitcrows are capricious and oppor-
tunistic scavengers. With feathers of crimson so deep it is
often mistaken for black, these large corvids are as likely
to help a wandering adventurer as they are to report that
adventurer to the local authorities. In fact, most pitcrows
will often do both, for double the reward.

coaxed, or coerced into working with others, they often
find themselves in scouting roles. Single crows might
stake out a building, crossroads, or grave, reporting their
observations to a clandestine employer in exchange for
choice scraps or jewellery. A demon lord or archdevil
might enlist a whole murder to scout battlefields or harry
routed enemies. Whatever the case, pitcrows do not seek
to put themselves in danger and can always be found
plucking at the viscera of corpses after a meeting of devils
and demons.

communities can grow surprisingly large and exhibit
a kind of mass self-governance. Any individual found
exploiting the common good is immediately ostracised
and assaulted. Defecate too close to the communal blood
pool? Get pecked to death. Exhibit a communicable dis-

you can protect? They get pecked to death.

months of age, a wyvnkin looks much like its parents,

Demonglass
Warriors
The demonglass found on the Western Frontier is the
solidified essence of the overlord Tol Kharash and his
lesser fiends. Cults of the Horned King—notably, the
denizens of Turakbar’s Fist—often embed small shards
of demonglass within the cult's warriors. This serves
as a minor form of possession, compelling the warriors
to serve the Horned King while simultaneously
weakening their ability to resist his fiendish minions.
The basic abilities granted by embedded demonglass
are presented in the Demonglass Warrior template,
while other potential powers are described in the
Demonglass Champion sidebar.
Removing an embedded demonglass shard from a
creature is a risky proposition, typically killing the host.
Removing a shard safely requires the host to either be
a willing participant, Restrained, or Unconscious. A
Remove Curse or Greater Restoration spell cast on the
host breaks the possession and allows the shard to be
removed. The actual physical removal requires a sharp
tool and a Wisdom (Medicine) check with a DC of 15; if
the check fails, the shard is still removed, but the host
suffers 15 points of Piercing damage.
Demonglass Warrior
Template
Beasts, Humanoids, Giants, and Monstrosities can
all become demonglass warriors if embedded with
a demonglass shard. When a creature becomes a
demonglass warrior, it retains its statistics except as
described below.

Set a Trap. The Tharashk hunter creates a magical
trap in an unoccupied space within 5 feet. A trap

hunter can choose one currently active trap to

that moved into the space. Failure: 13 (2d12) Piercing

following spells, requiring no Material components,
using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save

1/Day Each: Hunter’s Mark, Locate Object, Longstrider

the Incapacitated or Frightened condition, friendly

Actions
Multiattack. The westwind rider makes two Lance or
Longsword attacks, in any combination.
Lance. Melee Attack Roll: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit:
8 (1d10 + 3) Piercing damage. If the westwind rider
is mounted and directed its mount to move at least
10 feet straight toward a target immediately before
the hit, the target takes an extra 11 (2d10) Piercing
damage and, if it is Huge or smaller, it is pushed up
to 10 feet away and has the Prone condition.
Longsword. Melee Attack Roll: +5, reach 5 ft. Hit: 7
(1d8 + 3) Slashing damage or 8 (1d10 + 3) Slashing
damage if used with two hands.
Arcane Blast. Ranged Attack Roll: +4, range 120 ft. Hit:
13 (2d10 + 2) Force damage.
Reactions
Take Heart! Trigger: A creature that the westwind rider
can see, and who can see or hear the westwind rider,
is hit by a melee attack. Response: The target adds 2 to
its AC against the attack.
Wandslinger
A flamboyant duelist with a sharp tongue, this
wandslinger is always ready for the next challenger.
They could be a wand for hire traveling from town to
town. They might be a colorful caravan guard, or an
equally colorful brigand preying on caravans.

Actions
Multiattack. Diorite makes 3 Eldritch Bolt attacks. Up to
three of these attacks can be replaced by Stone to Flesh.
She also makes one Sculptor's Claws attack.
Sculptor's Claws. Melee Attack Roll: +7, reach 5 ft. Hit:
6 (1d4 + 4) Slashing damage, and the target must
succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have
the Restrained condition. The target can repeat the
saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the
effect on a successful save. If the target fails a saving
throw against this ability while it has the Restrained
condition, it instead has the Petrified condition. It can
continue to make saving throws at the end of each of its
turns, ending the petrification on a successful save.
Eldritch Bolt. Ranged Attack Roll: +7, range 120 ft. Hit: 9
(1d10 + 4) Force damage.
Stone to Flesh. Diorite ends the Petrified condition on
one creature she touches. Diorite regains 16 (3d10)
Hit Points and the newly un-Petrified creature has the
Charmed condition for 10 minutes.
Spellcasting. Diorite casts one of the following spells,
requiring no material components, using Charisma as
the spellcasting ability (spell save DC 15):
At Will: Blade Ward, Mold Earth XGE, Thaumaturgy
3/Day Each: Charm Person, Dispel Magic, Dissonant
Whispers, Earthbind XGE, Shield
1/Day Each: Dimension Door
Legendary Actions
Diorite can take 3 Legendary Actions, choosing from the
options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be
used at a time and only at the end of another creature’s
turn. Diorite regains spent Legendary Actions at the
start of her turn.
Diorite’s Fury. Diorite makes a Sculptor’s Claws attack
or an Eldritch Bolt attack.
Belief in Stone. Intelligence Saving Throw: DC 15, one
creature Diorite can see within 60 feet. Failure: 7 (2d6)
Psychic damage and the target believes one of its arms
has been turned to stone until the end of its next turn.
While affected, the creature cannot make use of that
arm or use an item it is holding with that arm (though it
can switch a held item to a different hand).
Whispers of Stone (2 Legendary Actions). Wisdom Saving
Throw: DC 15, each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere
centered on a point Diorite can see within 60 feet.
Failure: 7 (2d6) Psychic damage and is Frightened of
Diorite until the end of its next turn.
